annotations.note: Volume → part → treatise → chapter hierarchy. part is the top grouping level (mask=False, _UNMASKED). Treatises sit between part and chapter and are annotated as the 'translation' layer below (each treatise IS a translated work).

annotations.count_cue: 23 translated treatises, each opening with a bracketed translator credit '[Translated by <name>.]' on its own line just before the treatise body. Regex count of '\[Translated by' = 23 (verified programmatically). These are the English translations of Tertullian's Latin treatises (plus the appended Latin Acts of Perpetua & Felicitas) — the SUBSTANTIVE translated text that is the volume's reason for existing. Breakdown roughly matches the 3 part contents-lists: Apologetic ≈ 9 treatises (Apology, On Idolatry, De Spectaculis, De Corona, To Scapula, Ad Nationes, An Answer to the Jews, The Soul's Testimony, A Treatise on the Soul), Anti-Marcion ≈ 9 credits (Prescription Against Heretics, the Five Books Against Marcion, Against Hermogenes, Against the Valentinians, On the Flesh of Christ, On the Resurrection of the Flesh, Against Praxeas, Scorpiace, Appendix: Against All Heresies), Ethical/Appendix ≈ 5 (On Repentance, On Baptism, On Prayer, Ad Martyras, Of Patience) plus the 2 Perpetua-Appendix credits (Wallis's English version + the Latin Acts). Slight intra-part redistribution is because a few translators credit a sub-book; the bracketed-credit count, not the part contents-list, is authoritative.

annotations.note: PRIMARY diagnostic layer and the headline purpose of this gold: 'translation' is UNEXEMPLIFIED elsewhere in the corpus, and this critical edition supplies it cleanly. Each treatise is an English rendering of a Latin original, flagged by an explicit translator credit. mask=True per taxonomy (translated text is masked apparatus relative to the original-language body the detector would otherwise expect). Per-instance edges are not stored; presence + count (23) is the contract.

exemplars.note: Part Second's 'Introduction, by the American Editor' — a part-level editorial commentary essay ('The Second Class of Tertullian's works, according to the logical method I have endeavoured to carry out...'). Distinct from the 13-count Elucidation blocks; included as an exemplar to show the commentary layer also lives at part granularity.

annotations.note: type=commentary (mask=False, _UNMASKED — editorial commentary that is content the detector should KEEP, unlike masked apparatus). This is the second under-exemplified type this gold targets. Two sub-forms: (a) per-treatise 'Elucidations' appendices (13 blocks), (b) per-part 'Introduction by the American Editor' / 'Introductory Note' essays. The expected_count tracks (a) only; (b) is exemplified, not counted, to keep the cardinality honest. mask=False is correct here: gold_verify would flag mask=True against DEFAULT_MASK_BY_TYPE['commentary']=False.

annotations.count_cue: 5 'Introductory Notice'-titled editorial notices that head specific treatises/translations (regex count of 'Introductory Notice' = 5, verified programmatically). These are the translator/editor's prefatory NOTICES to individual works (e.g. Holmes's notice to the Anti-Marcion, the notice to the Five Books Against Marcion, the Perpetua & Felicitas notices). type=introduction (work-specific prefatory framing) is kept SEPARATE from the editor's evaluative 'commentary' (Elucidations) above and from the single CCEL set-introduction — the distinction: a 'Notice' introduces/contextualises a forthcoming text, an 'Elucidation' critically expands a finished one. Honest caveat: the introduction↔commentary line is genuinely fuzzy for the long Part-First 'Introductory Note' (which mixes biographical framing with the editor's evaluation); I classed the labelled NOTICES as introduction and the labelled ELUCIDATIONS as commentary, by their own headings, rather than re-judging tone.

annotations.note: type=introduction, mask=True (apparatus framing the translated text — contrast with commentary's mask=False). Five 'Introductory Notice'-titled blocks. The count is the literal heading count; their character is prefatory rather than evaluative, which is why they are introduction not commentary.

annotations.count_cue: Treatise sub-divisions ('Chapter I.', 'Chapter II.', …, mostly Roman-numeral, frequently with an em-dash title summary). The current detector segments 737 chapters across the 23 treatises (diagnostics by_type chapter=737, all numbered). This is FUZZY by eye: a line-anchored '\nChapter <roman>.' regex yields 870 occurrences, but that figure double-counts the per-treatise chapter-summary CONTENTS LISTS (each treatise prints its chapter titles as a forward-reference list before the translator credit, then again as in-body headings). The 737 detector figure is the de-duplicated in-body chapter count and is the honest navigational-container number; the 870 raw figure is recorded here as the upper bound including contents-list echoes. Per-canonical-treatise chapter counts vary widely (Apology 50, On Idolatry 24, Five Books Against Marcion run to many chapters per book) and are not independently re-tallied here.

exemplars.start_anchor: Chapter I.—Wide Scope of the Word Idolatry.
exemplars.note: In-body chapter heading: On Idolatry, Chapter I (em-dash summary form). Followed directly by the chapter's translated prose ('The principal crime of the human race...').

annotations.note: chapter is the grouping level BELOW translation (treatise) and ABOVE the masked footnote apparatus. mask=False (_UNMASKED). expected_count uses the detector's de-duplicated 737; the raw 870 line-count is the contents-list-inflated upper bound, documented honestly rather than picking a clean single number.

annotations.count_cue: Heavy critical-apparatus footnotes, interspersed after each chapter/treatise as numbered note lines of the form '<n>\xa0\xa0\xa0 <note text>' (newline + footnote number + three non-breaking spaces + space + text). Programmatic count of the regex '\n\d+\xa0\xa0\xa0 ' = 6280 (verified against reference_text(), not grep — the text uses \xa0 thin/nbsp glyphs). Numbering is CONTINUOUS across the whole volume (min 1, max 9186; the count 6280 < 9186 because numbering is per-treatise-resetting in places and some referenced numbers have no expanded note line). The notes carry scholarly cross-references, Latin source phrases, and editor remarks keyed to inline superscripts in the translated bodies.

annotations.note: PRIMARY masked layer alongside translation. mask=True per taxonomy. This 'Enhanced Version' interleaves the footnote apparatus inline after each chapter rather than pooling per-page, so the apparatus is content-anchorable (unlike the geometric idx101 case). expected_count is the line-count of expanded note entries (6280); it deliberately does NOT equal the max footnote number (9186) because numbering resets/skips — stated explicitly rather than forcing a clean number.
